data.title: Nvidia's stock clinches a stretch of weekly losses not seen since 2008
data.description:
By Hannah Pedone

One fund manager says the continued uncertainty makes Nvidia vulnerable to more selling, even as the stock has erased $1.16 trillion in market value in the past seven trading sessions

Nvidia's stock has been sinking amid corporate tumult in recent weeks.

Nvidia's stock booked declines for the seventh week in a row - a stretch of consecutive losses not seen in nearly two decades.

A cascade of factors has left the stock (NVDA) reeling - most notably former CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and the Nvidia board's investigation into whether he compromised national security or revealed corporate secrets.

On Friday afternoon, the stock extended its losses after Reuters reported that the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is probing Nvidia's accounting practices. Also on Friday, the New York Times reported that Alice Huang has ties through "family and associates" to China's defense industry. Jensen Huang previously admitted to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed who is suspected by U.S. officials of having been a Chinese intelligence asset.

But Nivida's stock had been under pressure prior to its CEO's downfall, with investors questioning the sustainability of artificial-intelligence demand.

Nvidia shares hadn't fallen for seven weeks in a row since July 2008, when the company issued a profit warning and was working to address defects in some of its chips.

Shares of Nvidia closed down 14% on Friday. They lost nearly 23% this week and are more than 47% of their peak close achieved in early October.

Nvidia's stock has fallen for seven trading sessions in a row, over which it has shed roughly $1.16 trillion in market capitalization. That's almost the size of Anthropic (ANT), which had a $1.18 trillion market capitalization as of Friday's close, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

By market value, Nvidia is now the fourth-largest U.S. company, falling below Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL) (GOOG) for the first time since April 2024, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Nvidia's market cap is now $3.03 trillion, while Alphabet's is at $3.24 trillion.

The stock's "weakness despite strong earnings shows how much it will take to restore confidence." David Miller, CIO at Catalyst Funds, told MarketWatch.

On Tuesday, Nvidia reported blockbuster earnings results and raised its revenue outlook for next year, but that wasn't enough to stem the bleeding.

Seaport Research analyst Jay Goldberg told MarketWatch that fund managers who previously held Nvidia because it was a "safety stock" are now "rotating out" amid the turmoil.

So what comes next?

Goldberg expects things to stabilize next week. "I don't think it keeps falling," he said - though adding that "there is no one in a hurry to buy it until we know who the next CEO is."

See also: Jensen Huang was a 'China salesman' for Nvidia. His exit is weighing on Chinese tech stocks.

But Catalyst's Miller said Nvidia's stock is "vulnerable" to more selling. The length of the losing streak alone "tells us very little about where the bottom is," he told MarketWatch.

"A sharp rebound is certainly possible, but I would want greater clarity on permanent leadership and the investigations, along with continued execution on customer demand and product deliveries, before becoming confident in a sustained recovery," he said.

In a Friday news conference, President Donald Trump said he would "like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back" to Nvidia.

"We have to protect our brilliant people. Jensen is one of them," Trump said.

-Hannah Pedone

AM Best Affirms Credit Ratings of Ameriprise Financial, Inc. and Its Subsidiaries

AM Best has affirmed the Financial Strength Rating (FSR) of A+ (Superior) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Ratings (Long-Term ICR) of “aa-” (Superior) of RiverSource Life Insurance Company (Minneapolis, MN) and its wholly owned subsidiary, RiverSource Life Insurance Co. of New York (Albany, NY). These companies represent the key life/health (L/H) insurance subsidiaries of Ameriprise Financial, Inc. (Ameriprise) (headquartered in Minneapolis, MN) [NYSE: AMP] and are collectively known as Ameriprise Financial Group. Concurrently, AM Best has affirmed the FSR of A (Excellent) and the Long-Term ICR of “a+” (Excellent) of Ameriprise Captive Insurance Company (ACIC) (Burlington, VT), a property/casualty (P/C) subsidiary of Ameriprise. In addition, AM Best has affirmed the Long-Term ICR of “a-” (Excellent) and the existing Long-Term Issue Credit Ratings (Long-Term IR) of Ameriprise. The outlook of all these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable. (Please see below for a detailed listing of the Long-Term IRs.)

The ratings reflect Ameriprise’s balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its strong operating performance, favorable business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

The balance sheet strength metrics for Ameriprise Financial Group remain supportive of the very strong balance sheet strength assessment. On an enterprise level, Ameriprise Financial Group has taken various steps to continue to de-risk its balance sheet from interest rate volatility, and this has been accomplished through reinsurance, reducing interest sensitive products and offering third-party alternatives for those products. AM Best views the capabilities of Ameriprise’s mature risk management program as being supportive of this strategy. Ameriprise Financial Group’s operating metrics include continued positive operating net income, sustained premium growth, and a high return-on-equity ratio which is well above industry averages. Distribution capabilities are robust throughout the group’s adviser channel as it continues to broaden its distribution reach, including through credit union and bank relationships. Ameriprise’s life and annuity business is complemented by the enterprise’s larger asset management businesses in the United States and internationally. The Ameriprise Financial Group is not only diversified geographically across the United States but also offers investment services in addition to life and annuity products.

The ratings of ACIC reflect its balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong as well as its strong operating performance, limited business profile and appropriate ERM. ACIC benefits from rating enhancement due to its strategic importance as a single-parent captive insurance provider.

AM Best assesses ACIC’s business profile as limited due to its narrow market focus as a single-parent captive serving just one customer (its parent) for a limited amount of exposure. ACIC provides various coverages to Ameriprise in the form of a blended management liability insurance policy, a workers’ compensation deductible reimbursement policy, fidelity bonds and property terrorism (conventional and nuclear, biological, chemical or radiological). The captive has generated strong operating performance as demonstrated by its five-year average pre-tax return on revenue and equity ratios, which compare favorably with the averages for AM Best’s commercial casualty composite. Additionally, ACIC benefits from a very low expense ratio.

data.title: DISA Partners with OADN Foundation to Invest in the Future of Nursing Education
data.description:
DISA Partners with OADN Foundation to Invest in the Future of Nursing Education

DISA Partners with OADN Foundation to Invest in the Future of Nursing Education

PR Newswire

HOUSTON, Nov. 20, 2026

Nursing Futures Initiative reflects DISA Global Solution's commitment to supporting the people and programs that prepare the next generation of healthcare professionals.

HOUSTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- DISA announced its partnership with the Organization for Associate Degree Nursing (OADN) and the OADN Foundation to launch the DISA Futures Initiative, a philanthropic effort focused on supporting nursing students and educators and strengthening the future nursing workforce.

Through the initiative, DISA will support OADN Foundation programs that advance student success, academic progression, faculty development, and opportunities for nursing educators, including those serving rural and underserved communities.

"The true power of philanthropy lies in the opportunities it creates and the lives those opportunities ultimately change," said Donna Meyer, MSN, RN, ANEF, FAADN, FAAN, President of the OADN Foundation. "DISA's generous investment will help nursing students and educators in need take the next step in their education and careers, with impact extending far beyond the scholarship recipients themselves. As they advance, they will educate future generations of nurses, strengthen patient care, and serve their communities. This lasting, collective impact is what makes this investment so meaningful."

The partnership reflects DISA's commitment to helping prepare students and professionals for the path from education to employment. By investing in nursing education, the initiative will recognize the people who are preparing and supporting the next generation of nurses and highlight the role associate degree nursing programs play in their communities.

"Healthcare readiness starts well before a student enters a clinical setting. It depends on strong nursing programs, dedicated educators, and students who have the support to keep moving forward," said Dave Dickson, Executive Vice President of Product and Executive Sponsor of the DISA Futures Initiative. "At DISA, we help institutions prepare students for clinical education and employment. The Futures Initiative gives us a way to put that belief into action alongside OADN, the OADN Foundation, and it's nursing students."

The OADN Foundation will independently administer scholarships, grants, and awards associated with the initiative, including eligibility, application review, and recipient selection. OADN and DISA will collaborate on awareness, storytelling, recognition, and sharing the initiative's impact.

"The Nursing Futures Initiative reflects what is possible when organizations come together around a shared commitment to the future of nursing," said Rick García, PhD, RN, CCM, FAAOHN, FAADN, FAAN, Chief Executive Officer of OADN and the OADN Foundation. "Associate degree nursing programs educate a significant portion of our nation's registered nursing workforce and are deeply connected to the communities they serve. DISA's investment will help us support students and faculty, create new opportunities for professional growth, and strengthen the pathways that sustain the nursing workforce."

A dedicated Nursing Futures Initiative webpage on OADN.org will provide information about the partnership, funding opportunities, award recipients, workforce insights, and program impact. Applications will continue to be administered through the OADN Foundation.

The initiative was formally introduced to the OADN community during the 2026 OADN Convention in San Antonio, Texas, from November 12-14, 2026.

About DISA

DISA empowers education institutions, hospitals, and health systems to prepare the next generation of students and professionals. Building on decades of pioneering leadership from CastleBranch (myCB) and American DataBank (Complio), we simplify student readiness through compliance, background screening, and onboarding, streamlining the journey from enrollment to employment.

Visit Website: https://disahealthcare.com/

About the Organization for Associate Degree Nursing

The Organization for Associate Degree Nursing (OADN) is the national voice and a leading advocate for associate degree nursing education. OADN advances excellence in nursing education and supports the faculty, administrators, students, and institutions that prepare registered nurses to meet the evolving healthcare needs of communities across the nation. Through advocacy, education, leadership, and community, OADN works to strengthen associate degree nursing education and the nursing workforce.

The OADN Foundation advances this mission through philanthropic investment in nursing students, faculty, innovation, academic progression, and initiatives that strengthen the future of associate degree nursing education.

Visit Website: https://oadn.org/

data.title: Tom Donald Adds Tokyo Honor to Growing List of Awards for Never Say Die
data.description:
Tom Donald Adds Tokyo Honor to Growing List of Awards for Never Say Die

Telly and festival honors spotlight a Bay Area filmmaker and musician whose career spans advertising and independent production

Bay Area filmmaker, musician and producer Tom Donald’s Never Say Die has earned its latest honor from the Tokyo Film & Screenplay Awards 2026, extending a run of recognition that includes a Telly Award and Best Music Video at the Los Angeles Film & Documentary Awards. Other honors include recognition from the Toronto Film Awards, Los Angeles Movie & Music Video Awards, Hollywood Stage Script Competition and Hollywood Best Indie Film Awards. The film screened September 9 at Oakland’s Grand Lake Theatre during the opening session of the 24th Oakland International Film Festival. Its official selections also include Bernal Heights Outdoor Cinema, the New York City Independent Film Festival and the Tokyo Lift-Off Film Festival.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120209521/en/

Tom Donald’s "Never Say Die" has earned its latest honor from the Tokyo Film & Screenplay Awards 2026, extending a run of recognition that includes a Telly Award and Best Music Video at the Los Angeles Film & Documentary Awards.

Behind the 3-minute, 32-second film is a creative career spanning decades of music, advertising and filmmaking. Donald, who turned 80 on September 6, drew on those experiences to write a song and make a film about mortality, persistence and taking full advantage of life’s opportunities.

“I think the real message of Never Say Die can apply to anyone, at any age. Take full advantage of your life and the opportunities that present themselves along the way,” said Donald.

Donald began as a musician with ambitions of becoming a rock star. Recording led him to writing and producing jingles, which introduced him to advertising agencies. His agency career included Foote Cone & Belding and Saatchi & Saatchi; writing for television led naturally to directing commercials. He subsequently established Tom Donald Films and later developed hiTrecords, his current content creation company.

Having worked in recording studios with tape machines he remembers as “the size of a small refrigerator,” Donald welcomes the possibilities of making records and films on laptops. The equipment has changed dramatically; his commitment to a good story has endured.

Donald also spent ten years teaching film at a San Francisco film school, where he emphasized collaboration from the first day of class. He credits the friends and family who helped make Never Say Die and shares the pride in its recognition with the team behind it. Today, Donald continues to work in his studio each morning, playing piano and other instruments, working at his computer and exploring ideas scribbled on yellow legal pads. The awards have arrived while he is already considering what to make next.

“One of those hunches will likely rise to the surface but what I can say almost unequivocally is that as much as I love Never Say Die, the next project will be completely different,” said Donald.

data.title: The hidden catch in Anthropic's IPO: Billions of locked-up shares are waiting in the wings
data.description:
By Michael Kramer

A looming oversupply problem could weigh on the stock over the next year

Members of Anthropic's board of directors appear at the Nasdaq exchange before Wednesday's IPO. Company insiders have billions of shares still locked up.

The Anthropic IPO thus far hasn't been great for investors who bought at the opening price of $111.50 on its first day of trading. It hasn't really even been that great for those who got bought at the offering price of $83, either. As of the close of trading Friday, the shares are trading at just $88.30.

Most investors never read an IPO prospectus, but they really should at least glance at Anthropic's (ANT). Probably one of the most important sections to read closely is the one on shares eligible for future sale. A quick look suggested the IPO could have issues once it started trading.

'Shares eligible for future sale'

The prospectus shows that the deal size was 980 million shares, and it grew to 1.127 billion after the underwriters exercised their option to buy another 147 million. That sounds like a big number, but with the company's 13.4 billion shares outstanding (page 20), the deal was only about 8.4% of the total company.

More importantly, it also shows that on the first trading day after the prospectus, up to 315 million shares of Class A stock (page 317) held by its non-founder directors, officers, and current and former employees and consultants were eligible to be sold. That comes to about 28% of the offering size.

Of course, that doesn't mean that everyone who had the chance to sell on Wednesday sold. There is no way to know how many of those holders sold, at least not right away, but the stock did trade 857 million shares on its first day of trading, so the deal didn't even turn itself over. But that volume alone doesn't tell us how many shares those holders sold.

But the issues don't stop there. From a liquidity standpoint, not only did 315 million shares already become available to trade on top of the initial offering size, but the prospectus also reveals that up to 303 million Class A and N shares come off lock-up on Dec. 15, another 303 million shares of Class A and N come off lock-up on Jan. 5, another 353 million shares on Jan. 19 and 353 million shares on Feb. 2. So, over the first 76 calendar days, about 1.6 billion shares will be eligible to be sold, taking the initial float of 1.127 billion and more than doubling it to about 2.75 billion.

Supply will continue to grow

Worse, on the second full trading day after it releases its earnings results for the year ended Dec. 31, 2026, another 1.7 billion shares come off lock-up. This lock-up release schedule continues over the next year, with more shares released roughly every two weeks after each earnings report, until all the shares are eligible to be sold. The numbers become a bit eye-watering.

None of this even considers whether the stock's fundamentals make sense or answers questions investors have had about the company's potential profitability, future spending commitments or debt burden.

Generally, when supply increases, price declines. So as more stock comes up for sale, the stock price may continue to drift lower if these holders choose to sell their shares. It adds up to quite a lot over time.

A balancing act

The prospectus states that after the offering and a concurrent private placement, and with the underwriters' option exercised in full, the company had roughly 7.73 billion shares of Class A common stock and 5.64 billion shares of Class N common stock, or about 13.4 billion in total. It also says that lock-up and market standoff agreements cover about 15.5 billion shares (page 21), a figure that counts shares issuable from stock options, restricted stock units and convertible notes. That means that roughly 15.5 billion shares, in total, can come off lock-up over time. Again, that doesn't mean they all come up for sale. They may never come up for sale, but it is still a lot of lingering supply and a potential overhang.

Over time, as the lock-up period unwinds and the shares settle, the market will come into better balance, where sellers and buyers can meet. The only question is at what price. At least from the outside, that price doesn't seem to be where the shares opened on their first day of trading.

If Anthropic's stock fails to live up to the hype, it may only be because there was simply too much of it.

Michael Kramer is the founder of Mott Capital Management and a long-only investor focused on macroeconomic themes. He analyzes long-term macro trends and short-term market risk using technical analysis, fundamentals and options-market positioning. See here for further disclosures.

-Michael Kramer

data.title: Everyone's making money off 'GTA 6' this week - except investors in Take-Two's stock
data.description:
By Bill Peters

'Grand Theft Auto VI' might be a blockbuster game, but investors are shrugging it off

"Grand Theft Auto VI" finally arrived this week.

Take-Two Interactive's "Grand Theft Auto VI" might be one of the biggest entertainment events ever, but investors haven't been impressed.

Shares of Take-Two (TTWO) - which owns Rockstar Games, the developer of "GTA 6" - are down around 8% over the past five days. While shares rallied on Wednesday, a day before the videogame's official release, they fell Thursday and rose just fractionally on Friday after official sales figures dropped.

Rockstar Games on Friday said first-day retail sales for the game had hit $3.79 billion. It said 32.5 million units sold pre-release.

"It's partly a sell-the-news moment," said Nick McKay, an analyst who follows the videogame industry at Freedom Capital Markets. "I think it's partly the fact that tech more broadly has been weak of late."

"GTA 6" has earned a near-perfect Metacritic score, drawing praise for its more mature storyline - a present-day Floridian twist on Bonnie and Clyde - and an immersive open-world experience. People have called in sick to spend time playing the game. Boyfriends have disappeared to tend to their in-game girlfriends. Some researchers have anticipated a spike in online food-delivery orders. Others have called the game a reflection of the garbled, unhinged state of the U.S. itself. Analysts, by and large, are optimistic about the game's prospects for years to come.

But McKay noted that "GTA 6" debuted the same week as Anthropic's (ANT) IPO, potentially steering some investors' attention away from the game. More broadly, the AI trade is a mess for multiple reasons, and AI advances, along with the cost-of-living squeeze, have posed a threat to the videogame industry.

Moreover, McKay said, investors and gamers' frustrations with Take-Two may have been building in the months leading up to the game's launch, as details about "GTA 6" remained sparse.

He said that people have been waiting for the game essentially since "Grand Theft Auto V" launched in 2013. But he said there was little news on "GTA 6" until about three months ago, when Netflix (NFLX) offered an extended look at the game in August. The game's release suffered from multiple delays. Ahead of "GTA 6's" debut, hackers also leaked footage of the game, exploiting the information vacuum, he said. Moreover, some data had shown that "NBA 2K27," which is part of Take-Two's other big videogame franchise, had underperformed.

"If we all assumed that 'GTA' would be a very well-reviewed game, and we assumed that it would perform well, you say to yourself, 'OK, well, what comes next?'" McKay said.

"We don't have really any information on when 'GTA's' going to launch on PCs, when 'GTA Online' is going to launch for the new game, so I think investors have started to look toward that," he added.

Shares of Take-Two are down 18% so far this year.

Oppenheimer analysts, in a note on Thursday, also suggested the game's realism was both a strength and a weakness.

"The more demanding police encounters, elaborate vehicle interactions, and everyday activities may slow gameplay and sometimes feel too laborious vs. 'GTA V,'" they said.

They also said the gameplay could be cumbersome at times. Clunky controls - for driving, fighting and other actions - "can occasionally break immersion." And they had questions over how any future online version of "GTA 6" might make money off of updates, add-ons and in-game purchases.

Morgan Stanley analysts, in a note on Thursday, said any post-launch press releases on sales figures from Take-Two could also serve as a "sell the news" event for the company's stock. Along with the launch of a PC version of the game, they, too, said investors' attention would soon shift toward how Take-Two and Rockstar can keep online players spending.

"Unlike the initial game purchase, this spending can recur over many years, as demonstrated over 'GTA Online's' 13-year history," they said. "We see the potential combination of a larger audience and higher monetization as an important driver of multi-year earnings growth, with strong launch sales establishing the foundation for the next decade of monetization."

McKay said that some Wall Street analysts who follow videogames were new to the space, and lacked historical context on how games tend to sell. Demand estimates were all over the place, and some were overly optimistic, making it difficult to please everyone, he said.

Sales for "GTA 5," he noted, spiked in the days after it hit shelves, but plateaued in the months after that initial rush. Just because an estimated 130 million to 140 million newer-generation PS5 and Xbox Series X|S consoles are in people's homes doesn't mean that many copies of "GTA 6" will be sold. And he said that few gamers were likely on the fence about whether to buy "GTA 6" at this point.

McKay pointed to other challenges for Take-Two and the rest of the industry. Shifts to digital and mobile gaming remain a threat. Consoles and other hardware are expensive. The industry's growing focus on mega-franchises - like "Grand Theft Auto" or "Call of Duty" - have threatened demand downstream. As those games gobble up more playing hours and dollars, other games can suffer, he said.

"What you see on the console side is games that would have been bigger sellers 10, 15, 20 years ago, when they launch now, the demand isn't there," he said. "Because consumers have said 'You know what? My money's going toward 'Call of Duty' now. Or, my money's going toward 'GTA.'"

-Bill Peters

data.title: LAIKA Takes Portland to the Movies This Thanksgiving
data.description:
LAIKA Takes Portland to the Movies This Thanksgiving

Portland studio celebrates its hometown and the extraordinary community support for WILDWOOD with complimentary screenings across the city on Sunday, November 29

This Thanksgiving, LAIKA is giving back to the hometown that helped bring WILDWOOD to life. On Sunday, November 29, the Portland-based animation studio will invite local audiences to enjoy complimentary screenings of its critically acclaimed film throughout the Portland area. Fifteen theaters have already signed on, offering more than 7900 seats across 37 screenings, with additional participating locations expected to be announced.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120376057/en/

LAIKA celebrates its hometown of Portland, Oregon.

Set in a fantastical version of Portland and handcrafted by LAIKA's artists in Oregon, WILDWOOD is a love letter to the city and its extraordinary creative community. Portland audiences have embraced the film with remarkable enthusiasm, making the city one of the standout markets for WILDWOOD nationally.

Now LAIKA is bringing that connection full circle, joining forces with theaters across Portland to celebrate the community that inspired the film and has supported it so enthusiastically. The screenings are part of a wider Thanksgiving homecoming celebration, which also includes a special WILDWOOD soundtrack event featuring Portland musician Colin Meloy at the Bagdad Theater on Friday evening, November 27.

WILDWOOD is a sweeping, handcrafted fantasy filled with magic, danger, heart, and wonder — made to be experienced together on the big screen. It is Certified Fresh with a 97% critics’ score and 96% Audience score (Certified Hot) on Rotten Tomatoes.

Seven of the film's ten highest-grossing theaters across the U.S. and Canada are right here in the Portland area, demonstrating the remarkable connection between LAIKA and its hometown.

“Portland isn't just where we make our films. It's part of who we are,” said David Burke, LAIKA’s Chief Marketing and Operations Officer and Executive Producer on WILDWOOD. “WILDWOOD was inspired by this city, brought to life by an extraordinary community of artists here, and embraced by hometown audiences in a way that has been incredibly meaningful to all of us. This Thanksgiving, we want to say thank you by bringing Portlanders together to share something special at the movies.”

After her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows, headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee) launches a desperate rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness—an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, Oregon. Joined by her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis (Jacob Tremblay), Prue navigates a world of talking animals, bandits, and powerful figures driven by grief and ambition. As the pair is drawn into a conflict threatening the balance of the forest itself, Prue must discover the strength and belief she never knew she possessed. If she hopes to save her brother and protect WILDWOOD’s fragile future, she will have to risk everything. From Oscar®-nominated and BAFTA®-winning LAIKA, WILDWOOD is a sweeping adventure about love, sacrifice, and the magic that reveals itself when we dare to look beyond the familiar.

Created by more than 1,200 artists and technologists, WILDWOOD represents an extraordinary achievement in handcrafted filmmaking. From its intricate puppets and costumes to its elaborate sets and fantastical landscapes, the film reflects the artistry, imagination and creative ambition that have defined LAIKA's work in Oregon for more than two decades.

COME HOME TO WILDWOOD – SUNDAY, NOVEMBER 29

Complimentary tickets will be available for screenings at participating theaters throughout the Portland area, with 15 locations and 37 screenings already confirmed. Additional locations and showtimes may be announced.

Audiences are encouraged to reserve seats in advance. For the latest participating theaters, showtimes and reservation information, visit www.WildwoodForPortland.com.

About LAIKA: Founded in 2005 and based in Oregon, LAIKA is an award-winning animation studio and Certified B Corporation driven to tell bold, original stories that stand the test of time. Renowned for its distinctive artistry, innovative filmmaking, and pioneering use of technology, LAIKA has redefined the possibilities of stop-motion animation.

The studio’s five films — Coraline, ParaNorman, The Boxtrolls, Kubo and the Two Strings, and Missing Link — were each nominated for the Academy Award® for Best Animated Feature. LAIKA’s latest animated feature, WILDWOOD, premiered on October 23, 2026, to critical acclaim. The studio has also expanded its storytelling into live action film and television.

Press Contact:

data.title: Anthropic's stock sees dramatic slide but manages to stay above its IPO price
data.description:
By Emily Bary

Anthropic's inability to hold its opening stock price has been seen as 'bad for the rest of tech'

Anthropic finished with a $1.16 trillion valuation on Friday.

There was no honeymoon period for Anthropic after its record-breaking initial public offering.

Shares of the AI company fell 9% on Friday, making for a gloomy second day of trading. At its lowest intraday point, Anthropic's stock (ANT) traded just five cents above its $83 IPO price, though it pared losses to finish at $88.30, still well below its $111.50 opening price.

It was a downbeat sign for the broader technology ecosystem as well, with AI stocks taking a beating across the board.

"The vast majority of this continued selling pressure in the last 24 hours feels more to do with" the Anthropic IPO than it does with some less-than-perfect earnings reports in the technology sector, Jefferies trading-desk analyst Jeffrey Favuzza wrote in a morning note to clients.

He added that Anthropic's inability to hold its opening price and the downward pressure in Friday's premarket action is being viewed as "bad for the rest of tech."

Anthropic's IPO was seen as a tentpole event for the AI trade. The company finished with a $1.29 trillion valuation on Thursday, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Friday's action brought that down to $1.16 trillion.

"Anthropic's strong debut alongside a falling technology sector suggests investors still believe in AI but are becoming more selective about what they will pay for that growth," David Miller, the chief investment officer at Catalyst Funds, said in emailed comments.

Some analysts initiated coverage of Anthropic's stock after Thursday's close, chiming in with mixed views.

Don't miss: After Anthropic's 'bittersweet' IPO, here's what lies ahead

"We are cautious, not negative," wrote Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg, who launched coverage of shares with a neutral rating.

He called Anthropic an "incredible company," but also one "asking for an incredible leap of faith by investors."

"We think the company will need time to grow into its valuation and answer some very big questions about its growth trajectory," he continued. For instance, the company saw 43% revenue growth from the second quarter to the third quarter. That compared with a much faster 144% growth rate from the first quarter to the second quarter.

Goldberg referred to that as a "worrying" deceleration. "To merit its valuation, it will need to see much higher growth rates over the next two years," he added.

William Blair's Arjun Bhatia was more upbeat, calling Anthropic a "generational company driving a generational technology shift" as he began his own coverage of the stock with an outperform rating.

"Questions about the future are worth asking, even those that don't have an answer at this point," he wrote.

But at the same time, he and his team "don't want to miss the forest for the trees."

"We think AI is a generational shift in the tech landscape, and Anthropic is leading the charge in developing AI with a select handful of other companies," Bhatia wrote. "Over the next decade, we think Anthropic is only going to become more important and consume a greater portion of enterprise spend," meaning it will command more of the budget that businesses have to allocate toward technology.

See also: Anthropic soared in its debut as stocks tanked. Only one other IPO has done that since 1990.

-Emily Bary
